persistence_invariants.brief: UNIQUE constraint on (sku, location); no two rows share the pair, so a repeat write updates in place rather than storing a duplicate (realizes R3, AC3).
sku, location, quantity and inventory_code are NOT NULL; a filed stock record always carries the full pair, quantity and combined code (AC1).
CHECK (quantity >= 0); a stored stock level is never negative (realizes the non-negative half of R2 at the schema level).

Initial create_table: after a single-step downgrade-then-upgrade the stock_records table with its columns and constraints is recreated (schema recreation semantics; there are no pre-existing rows to preserve on an initial migration).

open_decisions.question: Is stock_records the authority on whether a SKU/location is 'known', or does a later story need a separate SKU/location catalog with a foreign key? First filing establishes the pair here.
What composes the 'combined' inventory_code (e.g. sku+location+batch)? Stored as an opaque string for S1; a later story may need to decompose or derive it.

nfrs.fitness_function: an additive migration on the pre-existing stock_records table preserves every row created before it, and an inventory adjustment's timestamp and actor stay immutable once written.
fitness_functions: an additive migration on the pre-existing stock_records table preserves every row created before it (row survival applies only to additive migrations on an existing table, not the initial create_table)
an inventory adjustment record's timestamp and actor are immutable once written (no update path mutates them)

nfrs.fitness_function: a write that would store a negative quantity or overcommit beyond available quantity is rejected at write time; never a stored negative, never a silently-allowed double-allocation.
fitness_functions: a write that would store a negative stock quantity is rejected at write time (never a stored negative)
a pick that would overcommit beyond available quantity is rejected at write time (never a silently-allowed double-allocation)

nfrs.fitness_function: every (sku, location) pair is uniquely addressable; a repeat write for an existing pair updates in place so exactly one row exists, with no duplicate stored and no error surfaced (PI1).
the integration suite runs against the paired Lakebase branch via DATABASE_URL, not a mock or in-memory substitute; CI refuses to merge a PR whose integration tests do not run against a real branch.
the boundary layer returns JSON, not server-rendered HTML; the UI is a single-page React + TypeScript app under client/ that navigates client-side with no full-page reload.

imports point inward only (boundary -> service -> repository -> models) and the ORM session is confined to the repository; enforced deterministically by the consort-layering-clean gate (checkImportLayering + checkOrmContainment).
the DB connection is read from DATABASE_URL in the environment (no hard-coded connection string, database name untouched); enforced by the config-in-env gate.
a rejected write returns a clear validation message naming the offending field (not a bare 'bad request'), rendered inline in the SPA.
